criteria.notes: 11 words at 131.5px over four clean lines, a real tension rather than a topic label, Alaska named in the headline. criteria.notes: Real beat structure and the contact sheet reads as one composed sequence. Slide 02 pays the cover instantly. The turn at 07 is earned and the deck says out loud that the join is its own argument. Costs: slide 08 is reorderable and adds no fact, 04 and 06 could swap, and 05 and 06 still read similarly at feed size, which blunts the deck's strongest swipe.

criteria.name: Artwork craft & genuine detail
criteria.notes: The named repairs are real and visible: slide 04's lit board plane and desaturating haze, slide 09's slot with a back wall, grain, a lit jamb and a dark edge, the graded gold nose, the feathered reserve on large boxes. value_structure 9 of 9, all nine contacts clear the floor, drawn share 83 percent. Slide 06 is genuinely fine work and slide 05's twin bands are honest measured art. The ceiling is held down by slide 08's inert two thirds and its failed thread metaphor, the shared striped-block vocabulary on 01, 02 and 07, and slide 04's silhouette still descending through perspective so it reads chart-like at thumb. bespoke_check median 0.538 with max pair 0.641 is the worst structural figure in the recent ledger against 0.087, 0.127 and 0.167 on runs 38, 42 and 41.

criteria.name: Story-art fusion
criteria.notes: Art parameters encode the story's numbers and QA proves it rather than asserting it: 34 of 340 and 32 of 317 counted mark for mark at one shared 2.4706px scale, eight proud leaves for eight consecutive AI questions, five sewing stations with exactly one threaded, and an accession rule that refuses to draw a tick past the present because the FCC asked and proposed nothing. Held off a 9 because the bookbinding conceit is chosen rather than intrinsic and slide 08's thread fails to say the thing it was built to say.

criteria.name: Alaska authenticity & local relevance
criteria.notes: The Alaska hook is genuine and not a sticker: the FCC itself reaches for Alaska as its example, and the spine is two years of Alaska-specific counts from the primary record. But no Alaskan place, person, community, provider, carrier or borough is named anywhere in nine slides, and the visual world is a library shelf that could be in any capital. An Alaskan reading this sees their state counted by Washington and never sees their own town.

criteria.name: Insight density & factual weight
criteria.notes: Eight of nine slides add new verified specifics. Word counts in band. Derived figures are labelled derived on the slide, in the storyboard and in the first comment, and the killed list refuses seven tempting overreaches including the Method 3 inference. The one thin beat is slide 08, which adds no new fact though it carries the deck's sharpest sentence.

criteria.notes: Hero structure, atmosphere, palette family, hook archetype and continuity device all diverge from their windows and the storyboard argues each against the named prior decks. Reused subsystems are more than two: the type trio is No.38's exact set returning, the gold Polaris and the forget-me-not token are house furniture across four-plus decks, and the counted-unit census on 05 is structurally the move 40 and 41 already made. Plus the topic sits one day behind another rural-health deck.

threshold_note: config/scoring_rubric.yaml's iteration ladder sets the applicable threshold at 7.7 for a run past four revision rounds, with the instruction to ship the best version and flag the shortfall in the email. This run is far past four. Against the standing 8.3 house threshold the deck does NOT clear, and that shortfall is flagged.
one_sentence_fix: Rebuild slide 08 so the gold cord visibly passes THROUGH a pierced sewing station and out the other side, shot close enough that the block fills the dead upper right two thirds of the frame, because that one slide is simultaneously the deck's largest inert zone, its one admitted failed metaphor, and a contributor to the 0.641 max pair that drags the artwork score under 7.

showrunner_disagreement.finding: The scorer flagged slide 01's stamp 'FEDERAL REGISTER VOL 91 NO 167 . AUGUST 31, 2026' as a house date-rule breach, reading CLAUDE.md's 'never a bare August 10'.
showrunner_disagreement.resolution: NOT a breach, and not changed. config/brand.yaml blesses this form twice. voice.do line: 'Use the ordinal when no year follows; with a year use the plain form, August 27, 2026, which is what the source documents print.' And date_format.iso_is_still_correct_for: 'a PROVENANCE STAMP in a source list, where the date is a citation rather than a sentence.' This string is a provenance stamp carrying a year, so it is correct on both counts. The first scoring cycle read it the same way.
showrunner_disagreement.real_defect_underneath: The two rules are written far enough apart in brand.yaml that a careful reader can reach opposite conclusions, and caption_check reads copy.json's fields rather than rendered slide furniture. Logged as a Phase 12 candidate: state the stamp exemption in CLAUDE.md's own date sentence, and teach the date gate to read the render.

known_unfixed: The accession rule's ticks are bare, without the per-tick date and claim-id labels the deck header once promised. Nine labels in a 920px span needs either canvas text, which the slide contract forbids, or nine DOM labels that would carve nine holes in the rule's own band. The storyboard declares this honestly rather than claiming it.

20 to 21px mono citation stamps are below the 24px mobile floor deck-wide, so the citation apparatus is a full-size-only layer. 24px overruns the safe zone on the longest strings even at reduced letter spacing.
Slides 05 and 06 read similarly at feed size.
No Alaskan place, person or community is named anywhere in the deck.
Slide 08's gold thread reads as a loop over the block rather than a cord through a station.
Slide 06's body plate still shows a hard edge where the type reserve clips the leaf stack; the feather softens the plate but not the boundary where the art stops.
editor_notes_for_email: SHIPPABLE, BUT BY 0.09. 7.79 against the 7.7 iteration-ladder threshold that applies after four-plus revision rounds. Against the standing 8.3 house threshold this deck does NOT clear, and that shortfall is flagged here rather than buried. Zero hard fails, all thirteen checked and evidenced. Things worth knowing before posting. ONE: the honesty architecture is the best thing here and should be defended in the replies exactly as the aftercare says. The FCC ASKS and proposes nothing (nine questions, all interrogative, C25), the join between the two notices is Alaska.Ai's argument and not the FCC's (C26 and C27, stamped in frame on slides 07 and 08), and the 306 and the 90.0 percent are subtraction on the FCC's own printed figures rather than FCC wording. Do not let a commenter turn any of those three into something the Commission said. TWO: two mono stamps sit at exactly 4.5:1 worst-point contrast. They pass with nothing in reserve; any future darkening of those plates makes them a hard fail. THREE: the scorer called slide 01's 'AUGUST 31, 2026' a date-rule breach and it is not one. brand.yaml blesses the plain form with a year and blesses provenance stamps in a source list, and this string is both. The real defect is that the two rules sit far apart in brand.yaml and the date gate reads copy.json rather than the render, which is logged for Phase 12. FOUR: six defects ship unfixed and are listed in known_unfixed above. The one worth attacking next is that no Alaskan place, person or community is named anywhere in nine slides. This story's Alaska is a tally in a federal table, and no name from the state appears to answer it.
